decision: get is step 1's show renamed with a single change: the error for a mapping or list now says `use \`troupe config show PATH\` to print it`. The new show branches on the kind of node it finds
options: Rename show to get and add a new show
Keep show as the scalar printer and add a flag

decision: get and show both import the theatre and record pending hand edits (reconcile) before printing
reason: Step 2 says every command except history reconciles first. get must answer from the files as they are, and the hand edit is then recorded once

decision: YAML layout: 2-space indentation, lists indented under their key, minimal quoting, keys in document order, compact form for collections inside list items. Empty collections are written {} / []
reason: Matches the default indentation step 1 writes (FR-029), is the most common hand-written layout, and reads back as the same values. Block style cannot express empty collections

decision: D-22 revised during planning: <file> is computed from real paths (symlinks resolved, theatre resolved), with .. segments for files outside the theatre. Replaces the original choice of lexically normalised paths that did not follow links
options: Lexically normalised include path as written, links not resolved
reason: The loader already identifies every file by its real location (cycle detection), so this names the file a set would write. A theatre under a linked directory such as /tmp on macOS still gives .troupe/troupe.yml

decision: source_label = os.path.relpath(file.path, theatre.resolve()) with os.sep replaced by /
options: Keep the include path as written (needs a second path per file in the loader)
reason: relpath gives .. segments and never a leading ./. Keeping the as-written path would need the loader to carry a second path and would disagree with the file set writes to

decision: show SCALAR --sources prints the scalar as one YAML node with the comment (e.g. `0.2 # from .troupe/troupe.yml`). A text include becomes a top-level literal block
reason: The contract is silent here. The user asked where the value comes from, and YAML is the only form that can carry the comment and stay consistent with section output. Flagged to the owner as the least obvious choice

decision:
A CRLF text include is still shown as a literal block, with 
 replaced by 
, so it reads back with 
. This is the only exception to read-back. get still prints the exact bytes
reason: The contract explicitly says text includes are shown as literal blocks, and a literal block cannot hold CR. show's YAML is for reading; get remains the exact form

decision: One space before the # in the source comment
reason: The minimum YAML requires. The contract gives no column, and one space is predictable

decision: --sources is an option of show only. It may come before or after PATH; on get it is a usage error (exit 2)
Control characters other than tab and line breaks in text includes, non-UTF-8 text and non-string keys are declared out of contract and not tested
show's YAML is written by a new module config/view.py that walks the located tree directly. It reuses render.py's scalar spelling functions and does not reuse render_block
options: Own renderer walking the located tree
reason: Only the located tree knows each value's source. ruamel's quoting and comment rules differ from ours (it cannot put a comment on a block-scalar header), and tests would pin library behaviour. Callbacks would couple set's delicate write-back code to a read-only view

decision: A text include is always a literal block, even when it is a single line. If the text cannot be represented as a literal block it falls back to double quotes. Other strings containing \n become literal blocks
reason: The contract says text includes are shown as literal blocks; the fallback keeps the output valid YAML

decision: An empty main file prints {}. An empty YAML include prints as `key: null`, sourced from the included file
reason: Follows the loader's existing representation (step 1 D-5)

decision: CLI uses argparse subparsers: get with a required PATH; show with an optional PATH (nargs='?') and --sources (store_true)
reason: argparse accepts options on either side of the positional and rejects get --sources through the existing usage path

decision: show without --sources on a scalar returns format_scalar directly, so view is never called for a bare scalar
reason: Identical to get (FR-211)

decision: The get hint wording lives in one function, use_show_hint, in commands.py
reason: One place for the FR-202 wording (Principle IV)

decision: No foundational phase: both commands reuse existing code
reason: get reuses step 1's show code path; show adds only a new module

decision: User stories run strictly in order (US1, then US2, then US3). Until US2 lands, show temporarily dispatches to commands.get
reason: US1 frees the show name, and keeping this order means the full suite passes at every commit
